nodes.name: Carbon cloth pretreatment
nodes.procedure: A clean piece of carbon cloth (2 × 4 cm²) was taken and sonicated with acetone, deionized water, and ethanol for 15 min, respectively, and then transferred to a vacuum drying oven overnight to finally obtain the pretreated carbon cloth.
nodes.source_text: First, a clean piece of carbon cloth (2 × 4 cm²) was taken and sonicated with acetone, deionized water, and ethanol for 15 min, respectively, and then transferred to a vacuum drying oven overnight

nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe-LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1.5 mmol (0.4362 g) Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.5 mmol (0.2020 g) Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 10 mmol (0.6006 g) urea, 5 mmol (0.1852 g) NH₄F were dispersed into 35 ml of deionized water to obtain a clear solution. The solution was then transferred to a 50 mL polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) reactor together with the pretreated CC and heated at 120°C for 8 h. The samples were cooled to room temperature, then repeatedly cleaned with deionized water, and dried for an entire night in a vacuum drying oven. To eventually obtain CC@NiFe-LDH.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ce-doped NiFe-LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: Same procedure as CC@NiFe-LDH but with addition of 0.0087 g (0.02 mmol), 0.0261 g (0.06 mmol) and 0.0434 g (0.1 mmol) of Ce(NO₃)₃·6H₂O respectively to obtain CC@NiFeCe(1%)-LDH, CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH, CC@NiFeCe(5%)-LDH (%Ce refers to the molar percentage of Ce to the total molar amount of Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O and Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O).
nodes.source_text: 0.0087 g (0.02 mmol), 0.0261 g (0.06 mmol) and 0.0434 g (0.1 mmol) of Ce(NO₃)₃·6H₂O were added in the same way as above to obtain CC@NiFeCe-LDH with doping amounts of 1%, 3% and 5%

nodes.name: CeO₂ electrodeposition on NiFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: CC@NiFe-LDH/CeO₂ with different deposition times (10 min, 15 min, and 20 min) were prepared by electrodeposition. The electrolyte was 0.2893 g Ce(NO₃)₃·6H₂O, 0.1948 g NaCl and 100 mL deionized water. Ag/AgCl served as the reference electrode, platinum sheet served as the counter electrode, and CC@NiFe-LDH served as the working electrode. The deposition current density was 0.5 mA cm⁻² at 60°C, and the electrodeposited electrodes were placed in a vacuum drying oven at 60°C for drying.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show smooth layers of nanosheets uniformly and densely anchored to the carbon fiber surface perpendicular to the carbon cloth substrate for CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figures S1-S3 (Supporting Information) and Figure 1a, SEM images show the microscopic morphology of CC@NiFe-LDH, CC@NiFeCe(1%)-LDH, CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH, and CC@NiFeCe(5%)-LDH nanosheet arrays.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows interconnected nanosheets in CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH with smooth lamellar nanosheet shape and no particles or impurities detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used to analyze the catalyst's morphology. Similar interconnected nanosheets were observed in CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH after the introduction of Ce (Figure 1b; Figure S6, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows clear lattice stripes ascribed to the (012) plane of NiFe-LDH with crystallographic spacing of 0.25 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Clear lattice stripes were seen from the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images (inset of Figure 1b,d), which can be ascribed to the (012) plane of NiFe-LDH with a crystallographic spacing of 0.25 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental profiles demonstrate evenly dispersed Ni, Fe, O, and Ce throughout the nanosheets of CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Corresponding EDX elemental profiles (Figure 1e,f) also demonstrate the evenly dispersed Ni, Fe, O, and Ce throughout the nanosheets, again verifying the homogeneous doping of Ce in the lattice.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES measurement quantifies the specific amount of Ni, Fe, and Ce in the samples, demonstrating successful Ce doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: An ICP-OES measurement was performed in order to quantify the particular amount of Ni, Fe, and Ce in these samples (Table S1, Supporting Information), demonstrating the successful Ce doping and CeO2 modification.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows peaks at 11.4°, 22.97°, 34.43°, 38.99°, 59.94°, and 61.26° corresponding to (003), (006), (012), (015), (110), and (113) planes of NiFe-LDH; (012) peak shifts confirm Ce incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks at 11.4°, 22.97°, 34.43°, 38.99°, 59.94°, and 61.26° correspond to the (003), (006), (012), (015), (110), and (113) planes, respectively, of the NiFe-LDH (JCPDS card No. 40-0215).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines Cdl values of 4.09 mF cm^-2 for CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH, 2.92 mF cm^-2 for CC@NiFe-LDH, 1.66 mF cm^-2 for CC@NiFe-LDH/CeO2-15, and 1.16 mF cm^-2 for CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH/CeO2-15; ECSA of 102.25 cm^2 for CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Cdl value of CC@NiFe-LDH, CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH, CC@NiFeLDH/ CeO₂·15 and CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH/ CeO₂·15 are determined as 2.92, 4.09, 1.66, and 1.16 mF cm^-2, respectively (Figure 2e; Figure S15, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH exhibits lower Rct than CC@NiFe-LDH, indicating enhanced charge transfer ability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diameter of the Nyquist semicircle refers to the charge transfer resistance (Rct) of the catalyst ... CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH exhibits a lower Rct than CC@NiFe-LDH, suggesting an enhanced capacity to transfer electrons.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks shift to higher binding energies by 1.1 eV in CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH, higher Ni3+ percentage, positive shifts in Ni/Fe peaks indicating synergistic electronic interactions, and dominant Ce3+ species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH, the Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 peaks appear to migrate by 1.1 eV toward the higher binding energies ... all Ni 2p3/2, Ni 2p1/2, Fe 2p3/2, and Fe 2p1/2 underwent positive shifts, which suggests the presence of synergistic electronic interactions.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES Ni K-edge similar to NiO, Fe K-edge to Fe2O3; shifts to higher energies and changes in white line intensities indicate Ni/Fe lose electrons; Ce L3-edge shows mainly Ce3+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to Ni foil, the Ni K-edge XANES spectra are more similar to NiO ... The shift to higher energies in the Ni and Fe K-edge XANES spectra of CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH ... suggests that Ni, and Fe have lost electrons.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows similar octahedral structures for all samples; decreased coordination numbers indicate more oxygen/metal vacancy defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The K-space images of CC@NiFeCe(3%)-LDH ... do not show any significant change compared to CC@NiFe-LDH, which suggests that all of them have similar octahedral structures ... the coordination numbers ... were significantly decreased, which indicated that more oxygen vacancy defects and metal vacancy defects existed.
